Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
320 PM EDT Sun Sep 13 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Updated the Aviation and Tides/Coastal Flood discussion, as well
as Key Message 1 for latest observations and trends.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- 1) Some lingering showers through this evening before turning
  cooler with less humidity on Monday and Tuesday.

- 2) Increasing precipitation chances later in the week with an
  incoming cold front.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Some lingering showers through this evening 
before turning cooler with less humidity on Monday and Tuesday.

A pre-frontal trough was helping induce a few showers as of 
mid afternoon, but these should be increasingly disorganized 
and isolated/brief in nature. Humidity remains elevated, but 
overall forcing and instability are modest with increasing 
subsidence aloft.

Heading into tonight, an approaching cold front from the Great
Lakes may induce additional showers along and west of the
Allegheny Front as weakening storms approach from the Ohio
Valley. This threat should end around or shortly after midnight. 
Otherwise, this is largely a drier frontal passage which will 
also lead to cool temperatures and lower humidity to start off 
the work week.

Gradients on Monday are rather tight for mid-September as a 
broad 1024-mb surface high approaches from the Great Lakes. This
will favor a breezy northwesterly wind for Monday, with gusts 
up to 20 to 25 mph at times. Forecast highs are in the mid 70s 
to low 80s (5 to 15 degrees cooler for mountain locales).

As the seasonably strong dome of high pressure settles over the
northeastern U.S. Monday night, low temperatures plunge into 
the upper 40s to 50s. The autumnal feel to the air lingers into 
Tuesday before an eventual warm up by mid-week. Plenty of 
sunshine can be expected each day, but with decreasing winds on 
Tuesday with the ridge along the Eastern Seaboard. This all 
comes with dew points in the upper 40s to mid 50s which is 
certainly a change from recent days.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Increasing precipitation chances later in the week 
with an incoming cold front.

Upper-level ridging could continue into Wednesday, then begin 
to break down as a trough forms over the Hudson Bay. A stemming 
cold front tracks east over the Mid-Atlantic during the later 
half of the week, bringing increasing humidity as well as shower
& thunderstorm chances. There is still some uncertainty in the 
timing of any precipitation, but generally there should be 
increasing cloud cover by Thursday with a potential for showers 
& thunderstorms between Thursday and throughout the weekend as 
the front moves through. Severe probabilities continue to look 
minimal for this period.

Temperatures rise back into the mid-to-upper 80s across the region 
through Friday, then drop again in the wake of the front heading 
into the weekend.

&&

.AVIATION /19Z SUNDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Have removed thunder from the TAFs given increasingly shallow 
convection now producing minimal lightning thanks to increasing
subsidence aloft. Otherwise, VFR is expected through Monday 
night. Winds turn N/NW Monday and gust 20-25 kts.

VFR conditions and lighter winds then continue Monday night through
Tuesday as high pressure builds over the region. Winds shift to
the east and southeast Tuesday into Tuesday night.

Prevailing VFR conditions are expected to persist through Thursday 
and Friday. During the afternoon & evening hours throughout this 
period, a passing cold front could bring temporary low CIGs at 
terminals as a few showers and/or thunderstorms move through the 
region. Southerly winds shift northeasterly on Friday.

&&

.MARINE...
A pop up shower or storm can't be ruled out through early this
evening. A cold front arriving early Monday is forecast to 
yield increasing northwesterly winds with gusts up to 20 to 25 
knots. Small Craft Advisories have been issued from early Monday
morning into Monday night. Multiple wind shifts take place on 
Tuesday as high pressure passes by to the north. However, gusts 
drop off back into the 5 to 10 knot range, generally out of the 
east to southeast.

Winds stay below SCA thresholds through Friday. Southerly winds 
shift northerly by Friday afternoon in the wake of a cold front, 
which could bring a few showers and/or thunderstorms over the waters 
between Thursday & Friday evening.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Tide levels will remain elevated tonight, with Annapolis,
Alexandria, and Havre de Grace possibly approaching minor.

&&

.LWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
DC...None.
MD...None.
VA...None.
WV...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory from 4 AM to 10 PM EDT Monday for 
     ANZ530>533-535-536-538>542.
     Small Craft Advisory from 4 AM Monday to 7 AM EDT Tuesday for 
     ANZ534-537-543.

&&

$$

MARINE...LFR/BRO/DHOF
TIDES/COASTAL FLOOD...DHOF
